summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 5 upside misses — ANET +8%, WDC +7%, NTAP +6%, RMD +6%, AMD +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (ORLY -6%, AZO -6%, STZ -5%, ARE -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: ANET (+7.61%) — BlackRock named ANET a top-30 AI stock and it rode continued momentum from its new 1.6T AI-networking platform launch and raised 2026 outlook. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — ANET is a large-cap networking-equipment/AI-infrastructure name that isn't in the covered tech/momentum universe, so no filter ever saw it to include or exclude.

top_movers.catalyst: BlackRock named ANET a top-30 AI stock and it rode continued momentum from its new 1.6T AI-networking platform launch and raised 2026 outlook.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ANET is a large-cap networking-equipment/AI-infrastructure name that isn't in the covered tech/momentum universe, so no filter ever saw it to include or exclude.
top_movers.suggestion: Expand the tech-sector universe to include AI-infrastructure/networking-equipment names (e.g. ANET, and peers) alongside chips/hyperscalers so sector-driven rallies like this are captured.

top_movers.catalyst: AI-storage supercycle: BofA/Cantor/Melius hiked WDC targets ($732-$1,050) on tight HDD supply and 2026 capacity fully booked, sparking a dip-buying rally after last week's AI-hardware selloff.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — WDC's price (~$578, 52-wk range $64-$800) and realized volatility (250% YTD, ~14% intraday range today) likely place it above a max-share-price or max-ATR/price threshold used to size and gate the tradable list.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a periodic universe-refresh rule that re-admits names once trailing 20d ATR/price falls under the strategy's vol cap, so re-rated high-flyers like WDC aren't permanently excluded after crossing the price/vol ceiling.

top_movers.catalyst: Broadcom announced an expanded custom-chip/wireless partnership with Apple through 2031, easing customer-concentration fears and sparking a broad semi-sector rally.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AVGO is a mega-cap AI/semiconductor name likely excluded by a sector-cap or single-name concentration rule rather than a technical filter, since no bot universe currently includes it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AVGO to the AI-semiconductor sector bucket in at least one large-cap momentum universe so partnership/contract-announcement gaps in this name become tradable.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh same-day news; likely continuation of the post-Q4-earnings AI-storage re-rating (stock +48% YTD, still digesting late-May's 27-35% earnings pop) amid a broader AI-infra sector bid.
top_movers.miss_reason: NTAP sits outside any active strategy's tradable universe entirely — a large-cap enterprise storage/hardware name not on the sector/watchlist these bots cover, so no filter ever evaluated it regardless of today's move.
top_movers.suggestion: Add NTAP (and peer AI-storage names like PSTG, WDC) to the tech-hardware/infra universe given their post-earnings volatility profile now qualifies them under the existing large-cap liquidity threshold.

top_movers.catalyst: Extending oversold bounce after Goldman Sachs added RMD to its APAC Conviction List (~7/2); GLP-1/Philips competitive fears from Morgan Stanley's prior downgrade fading ahead of Aug 6 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RMD is a large-cap ($40B+) medical-device/sleep-apnea name that simply isn't in the region's covered sector list, so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add med-device/healthcare large-caps (RMD, peers) to the us universe watchlist so analyst-upgrade-driven oversold bounces get scanned by a mean-reversion or news-reactive strategy instead of being invisible entirely.

top_movers.catalyst: Goldman Sachs hiked PT to $640 (from $450) and Citi added AMD to its upside catalyst list; broad semis rally plus Turing AI GPU deal news added momentum.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AMD is a mega-cap, high-beta AI-chip name (>150% YTD, 75x fwd P/E) likely excluded by a market-cap/valuation-extension or sector-concentration cap keeping bot exposure to semis limited to names like NVDA already held.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a headline-catalyst watchlist rule: mega-cap semis on analyst-upgrade gap-ups ≥5% at open get a same-day universe-inclusion override, independent of the static valuation/cap filter.

top_movers.catalyst: ORLY offered ~$10B cash for Genuine Parts' auto-parts division; market punished the acquirer on deal cost/integration risk (GPC jumped ~13%).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ORLY is a mega-cap ($70B), low-beta auto-parts retailer that rarely moves >2%/day, so volatility/momentum-based universe construction never onboarded it as a frequent mover.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a same-day M&A-acquirer overlay: any S&P 500 name with a live deal headline (>$1B, 'to acquire/offers for') and same-day move >=5% gets temporary universe inclusion for the news-reactive strategy, independent of its static volatility screen.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued post-earnings overhang: May 26 Q3 revenue miss + tariff-driven margin pressure on auto-parts imports, compounded by O'Reilly/Genuine Parts M&A chatter roiling auto-parts retail sector.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AZO's ~$3,000/share nominal price (company has never split the stock) likely trips a max-price-per-share or lot-sizing filter, and its specialty-retail auto-parts sector may not map to any strategy's covered sector list.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a price-agnostic dollar-notional entry path (or explicit high-price whitelist) so strategies aren't gated by a max-share-price filter, and add specialty-auto-retail to at least one sector-coverage universe.

top_movers.catalyst: No single fresh headline: continued bleed from Jun 30 earnings (EPS beat but soft FY organic sales guidance -1%/+1%), capped today by a 50/200-day death cross triggering technical selling.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — STZ is a large-cap alcohol/beverage staples name, a sector likely excluded from momentum/growth-focused universes and too low-beta/low-volume-surge to trip catalyst scanners.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a staples/beverage large-cap bucket (or explicitly whitelist STZ) with a technical-breakdown tag (50dma<200dma cross) so death-cross days get flagged even absent a same-day news catalyst.

top_movers.catalyst: No same-day news catalyst found; move extends ARE's ongoing slide as a life-science REIT hit by falling occupancy (87.7%→88.5% guided), ~30% FFO decline, and a 45% dividend cut this year.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ARE is a large-cap life-science/biotech office REIT, a sector typically excluded from momentum/news-reactive equity universes since REITs trade on occupancy, FFO, and rate-sensitivity rather than typical earnings/momentum signals.
top_movers.suggestion: If REIT coverage is desired, add a separate rate-sensitive REIT sleeve using FFO-guidance revisions and occupancy trend as triggers rather than forcing ARE into the standard momentum/news-reactive universe filters.
